ingredients.name: Freshly grated coconut
ingredients.notes: about 2.5 cups; fresh is strongly preferred over desiccated -- it gives a much better melt-in-the-mouth texture

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: 1/3 cup; just enough to dissolve the sugar

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon; adds richness and a slight glossy sheen

ingredients.name: Vanilla essence
ingredients.notes: optional; or use rose water for a more floral aroma

ingredients.name: Full-cream milk powder
ingredients.notes: optional; some recipes use condensed milk instead of plain sugar for extra creaminess

steps.instruction: Grease an 8-inch (20cm) square tin or tray with butter and set aside near the stove. Prepare a bowl of ice water with a candy thermometer if available.
Add the sugar, water, and a pinch of salt to a heavy-bottomed saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely.
Add the grated coconut, butter, milk powder (if using), and vanilla. Mix well to combine. Continue cooking over medium-low heat, stirring continuously, for 20-30 minutes.

As the mixture cooks, the coconut will absorb the sugar syrup and the mixture will gradually thicken and pull away from the sides of the pan. Test for readiness: draw a spoon through the centre -- if the line stays without filling back in, the mixture is ready. On a thermometer, this is around 118-121C (245-250F / firm ball stage).
If making bicolour coconut rock (the traditional festive presentation), divide the mixture into two bowls at this point and add a drop of pink or green food colouring to one portion.

Working quickly, pour the mixture (or both colours side by side) into the prepared greased tin. Spread evenly with a greased spatula. Score into squares or rectangles with a greased knife while still warm.

Leave to cool and set at room temperature for 30-40 minutes. Once firm, cut along the scored lines and remove pieces from the tin. Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against serendibkitchen.com, lonumedhu.com, foodvoyageur.com, rotinrice.com, infolanka.com, milkmaid.lk, app.ckbk.com (Peter Kuruvita), and dailyfoodrecipes.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 9+ independent sources; very strong agreement on the sugar-dissolve-then-add-coconut technique and the line-in-pan readiness test
notes: Coconut rock (pol toffee, coconut candy, coconut ice) is considered one of the simplest and most universally loved Sri Lankan sweets -- it requires only three core ingredients (coconut, sugar, water) and no specialist equipment. The bicolour presentation (white and pink, or white and green) is the traditional festive version and appears consistently across sources as the standard New Year presentation. Fresh grated coconut is strongly preferred over desiccated by multiple sources -- hungrylankan.com explicitly notes that desiccated coconut leaves a dry residue in the mouth that fresh coconut does not. The line-test (drawing a spoon through the centre and seeing if the gap stays open) is the most consistently cited doneness indicator across all sources; a candy thermometer reading of 118-121C is the objective equivalent. The total_time_min includes 30-40 minutes of cooling time.
